transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Objective: POC scoping for Lattice Corp - define security gates and load/benchmark plan for 4-week pilot.
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO), Aisha (Platform), Ben (InfoSec), Sofia (SRE)

AutoSummary: Agree on SOC2/ISO as mandatory gating, SSO via SAML for pilot users, RBAC for tenant isolation, audit logs retention 12 months, KMS integration for keys. Pilot target: 500 QPS read-heavy retrieval + 30 QPS generation, median latency < 120ms end-to-end for retrieval, p95 gen <= 800ms, stable throughput at 90% utilization for 4-hour soak. Benchmarks: week2 smoke + perf run, week4 acceptance tests.

Timestamps and transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro and then go through the POC goals, security gates, and the load profile you guys want to validate
[00:12] Carlos: thanks maya, from our side i'll kick off — we're Lattice, building a knowledge assistant that connects internal docs and customer data, primary ask is low latency and strict auditability, we also have some residency rules for eu data
[00:27] Maya: got it. quick intros — jordan is our solutions engineer, he'll run through sizing and the benchmark plan
[00:37] Jordan: hey all, i'll be focused on throughput, batching and the harness. one thing up front — are you planning to run on Redwood Hosted or Private?
[00:47] Aisha: ideally private first, we need VPC peering and control plane separation. for the pilot we can do private in our aws account or bring your on-prem box, depends on the security review
[01:00] Ben: from infosec perspective our must-haves: SOC 2 evidence, ISO 27001 cert, SSO via SAML with our identity provider, RBAC for role separation, tamper-evident audit logs, encryption at rest with our KMS, and the ability to export audit trails for 12 months
[01:18] Jordan: ok that's helpful. Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC in the console, audit logs are available via streaming to S3 or pushed to your SIEM via syslog. we also have KMS integrations — support for aws-kms and customer-managed HSM in the private deployment.
[01:34] Sofia: timing question — we need to know the effort to enable VPC peering and KMS mapping. can't afford multiple weeks of waiting for infra changes during the pilot
[01:43] Maya: typical private checkbox is about 5 business days to set up peering and VPN, if we have IAM contacts and an initial VPC CIDR map. we'll aim to compress to 3–4 days for a pilot with SRE help
[01:55] Carlos: critical for acceptance: we require p99 <= 1.2s for user-facing chat flows and audit logs streamed within 30 minutes. if logs are delayed beyond that we fail the gate
[02:09] Jordan: noted. for generation models we usually see p95s in the 400–900ms range depending on model and sequence lengths. can you give us typical request sizes?
[02:20] Aisha: our traffic mix is about 85% retrieval queries (embedding-based rerank + short generation for snippets) and 15% long-form generation, average token context ~ 600 tokens for conversation history. target throughput spike 500 QPS retrieval, sustained 200 QPS, and 30 QPS generation with bursts to 60 QPS for short windows
[02:41] Jordan: that's helpful. for sizing we'd likely recommend a mixed pool: quantized LLM variant for generation and a smaller embedding/rerank pool. estimate: for 30QPS gen with 600-token contexts and p95 ~700ms you'd need roughly 4 high-memory/8 GPU slices in our dedicated pool or equivalent private nodes — we'll size precisely after we run a smoke test
[03:05] Ben: about SOC2/ISO, can you provide the control mappings and evidence? we need to complete our vendor assessment in two weeks
[03:13] Maya: yes — i'll send our SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestation, and a control matrix showing how Redwood maps to common frameworks. expects by 2027-04-06. Jordan will also include architecture notes for private deployment and KMS options
[03:29] Carlos: benchmarks — we want to measure latencies, KV cache hit rates, batching efficiency, and cost per 1k tokens. acceptance baseline should include throughput stability at 90% capacity for a 4-hour soak test. is that doable?
[03:42] Jordan: yes. our benchmark harness will collect p50/p90/p95/p99, token/sec, effective batch sizes, and memory metrics. we can run incremental tests: smoke (week 1), perf run (week 2), soak (end of week 3), and final acceptance run at week 4.
[03:58] Sofia: what about data residency? some docs are EU-only — can Redwood pin the model to eu region and keep that traffic local?
[04:07] Jordan: with private deployment in your VPC, traffic stays in your region. for hosted we have region pinning too but hosted adds more compliance questions. private is the cleanest for residency and KMS control.
[04:19] Maya: i'll note the pilot plan timeline: week 0 (this kickoff and infra prep), week 1 smoke + functional validation, week 2 perf benchmarks and tune, week 3 soak and regressions, week 4 acceptance and handoff. does that align with your expectations?
[04:33] Carlos: yes that timeline works. two asks — one: make sure RBAC can support our teams (admin, app-team, analyst) with least privilege. two: we need immutable audit logs exported to our S3 bucket and accessible via Athena.
[04:47] Jordan: RBAC is role-based with scopes per model and token. we can map your AD groups to roles via SAML assertions. audit logs can stream to S3 in newline-delimited JSON, and we support Glue/Athena-friendly formats.
[05:03] Ben: retention — 12 months is our baseline. also, we require proof that logs are tamper-evident and have a rotation policy for keys.
[05:12] Jordan: for tamper-evident logs, we support signed log entries and can ship a digest to your key-managed HSM daily. key rotation is supported by AWS KMS schedules and we can document the process.
[05:23] Aisha: on the performance side, what are the typical batching strategies? we want low latency for chat but also need to optimize cost for high throughput embedding lookups
[05:32] Jordan: Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching with dynamic thresholds; for chat we have latency-pref policy which limits batching windows and keeps p50 low, for embeddings we encourage larger batch windows and caching. KV cache reduces repeated context decoding for long conversations. we'll tune policies in week 2 perf run.
[05:50] Carlos: pricing and cost visibility — we need token-level cost estimates during pilot. can you provide a cost dashboard or at least a breakdown per model variant?
[05:59] Maya: yes we have a token-level dashboard in the console and Jordan can extract per-run cost estimates from the benchmark runs. we'll share a sample cost spreadsheet with expected unit economics for the pilot workload.
[06:12] Sofia: any blockers for running the perf harness from our side? we can run the client but would prefer Redwood to orchestrate the runs and push results into our S3 with CloudTrail enabled
[06:21] Jordan: we can orchestrate from our side or hand you the harness. recommended: run orchestrated with our SE in the loop for the first perf run to speed up tuning. we'll push results to your S3 and enable CloudTrail in the private control plane for audit.
[06:36] Ben: about data deletion and retention — if we request temporary artifacts be destroyed after the pilot, what's the process?
[06:44] Maya: in private deployments you control data lifecycle; we provide APIs and documented deletion playbooks. for hosted we have a documented process for data purge requests and retention windows. we'll include that in the docs pack.
[06:58] Carlos: success criteria recap: 1) security gates met (SOC2/ISO evidence + SAML SSO + RBAC + 12mo audit logs), 2) perf targets: p99 chat <= 1.2s, p95 gen <= 800ms, throughput stability at 90% utilization for 4 hours, 3) residency & KMS confirmed, 4) cost estimates within budget threshold TBD.
[07:20] Maya: perfect. to make the acceptance unambiguous we'll capture the exact measurement scripts and thresholds in the acceptance doc and share with you before the week2 perf run.
[07:30] Aisha: timeline notes — we need the SOC2 artifacts fast to unblock legal vendor review, and our infra team needs the VPC peering details this week to avoid delaying week1.
[07:41] Maya: action items noted — i'll send docs and a VPC checklist after the call. jordan will share the harness and an initial sizing spreadsheet.
[07:49] Jordan: one technical note — given 600 token contexts, KV cache hit rate has big impact on gen latency. for the perf run we'll include a synthetic trace that mimics conversation history growth so cache behavior is visible in metrics.
[08:06] Sofia: ok great. can we schedule a 45 minute on-prem checklist session next tuesday? Ben and Aisha will attend
[08:13] Carlos: next tuesday works for us. also please include a short demo of how RBAC and audit logs look in the console
[08:20] Maya: will do. next steps captured. any final questions?
[08:24] Ben: one more — do you support SAML with scoping attributes to limit model access? we want to ensure analysts can't call higher-cost models
[08:31] Jordan: yes we map SAML attributes to role scopes and can enforce per-role model allowances and rate limits. we'll include example SAML metadata in the docs.
[08:40] Carlos: thanks everyone. excited to see the smoke and perf runs.
[08:44] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and sample harness. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: some transcribed product names slightly off (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes typed as "k v cache"), minor speaker overlap at times.

End of transcript.
